title: Web <-> Mobile conversion (canonical)
content:
## What is platform conversion?

Emergent lets you **convert any app between web and mobile** at any time. When you convert, the platform rebuilds your app for the target platform — translating UI frameworks, layout patterns, navigation and platform-specific idioms — while preserving your app's logic, data and functionality.

Conversion is **non-destructive**: your original app remains intact until you confirm the converted version works as expected.

<Info>
Conversion works in both directions: web → mobile and mobile → web. The process is identical; the platform automatically detects your current deployment target and offers the opposite.
</Info>

---

## How conversion works

<Steps>
<Step title="Choose Convert from the deployment menu">
Open your app, click the **Deploy** dropdown in the top bar and select **Convert to [Mobile/Web]**.
</Step>

<Step title="The platform analyzes your app">
Emergent inspects your codebase, data schema, API routes, authentication flows and UI components to understand what needs to change.
</Step>

<Step title="Agent rebuilds for the target platform">
A dedicated conversion job runs — rewriting components, restructuring navigation, swapping frameworks (e.g. React web → React Native, or vice versa) and adjusting layout for the new form factor.
</Step>

<Step title="Review and test the converted app">
The converted app opens in preview mode. Test thoroughly — UI, navigation, data persistence, authentication and integrations — before deploying live.
</Step>

<Step title="Deploy when satisfied">
If everything works, deploy the converted app. If issues arise, iterate in chat ("the login button is misaligned on mobile") or revert to your original deployment.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Conversion is a Job">
Like any build task, conversion runs as a [Job](/what-is-a-job) and consumes credits. You can watch progress, pause or cancel if needed.
</Tip>

---

## Will I lose data or functionality?

**Short answer:** No — with caveats for platform-specific features.

### What carries over seamlessly

- **Database schema and data**: tables, relations, indexes and all stored records remain intact.
- **Authentication & user accounts**: login methods (email, OAuth providers) and user sessions persist.
- **API routes & server logic**: backend endpoints, webhooks and integrations continue working unchanged.
- **Environment variables & secrets**: all config, API keys and feature flags transfer.
- **File uploads & storage**: user-uploaded assets remain accessible (paths may adjust for mobile).

### What adapts automatically

- **UI components**: buttons, forms, modals and lists rebuild using platform-native patterns (e.g. web `<button>` → React Native `<Pressable>`).
- **Navigation**: web routing (URL-based) converts to mobile navigation stacks/tabs; deep links are preserved where possible.
- **Responsive layout**: desktop multi-column layouts condense to mobile-friendly single-column or tabs.
- **Form validation & input types**: web HTML5 inputs map to appropriate mobile keyboard types and pickers.

<Note>
The agent preserves **business logic** and **user flows** — the *what* of your app — while rewriting *how* it renders and navigates on the new platform.
</Note>

### What may require adjustment

<Warning title="Platform-specific features need review">
Capabilities unique to one platform (browser APIs, mobile sensors, OS-level integrations) may not translate directly. Test these carefully.
</Warning>

| Feature | Web → Mobile | Mobile → Web |
|---------|--------------|--------------|
| **Camera/microphone** | Works on mobile; may need permission prompts added | Web uses `getUserMedia` API; works in modern browsers |
| **Push notifications** | Needs mobile push service (FCM/APNs) configured | Web uses service workers; requires HTTPS |
| **Geolocation** | Native mobile APIs are faster/more reliable | Web `navigator.geolocation` works but less precise |
| **File system access** | Mobile uses app-sandboxed storage | Web limited to downloads folder or File System API (Chromium) |
| **Print/PDF export** | Not a mobile pattern; may need redesign | Works natively in browsers |
| **Right-click menus** | Touch-and-hold patterns replace | Standard context menus supported |
| **Hover states** | Touch doesn't have hover; replaced with press/active states | Hover works normally |

<Info>
If your app relies heavily on a platform-specific feature, mention it explicitly in chat during conversion: *"Keep the QR scanner working on mobile"* or *"Preserve the print invoice button for web."*
</Info>

---

## Common conversion scenarios

<AccordionGroup>
<Accordion title="I built a dashboard on web. Can I convert it to mobile?">
Yes. Multi-column layouts will condense to scrollable single-column or tabbed views. Charts and tables adapt to smaller screens (the agent may introduce horizontal scroll for wide tables or summary cards for dense data).
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="My mobile app uses camera scanning. Will that work on web?">
The web version will use the browser's camera API (`getUserMedia`). It works on HTTPS sites in modern browsers but won't have the same native feel. Test thoroughly; you may want to hide the feature on web or offer an upload alternative.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="What happens to my analytics/tracking code?">
Third-party scripts (Google Analytics, Mixpanel) typically carry over. Web tags remain in `<head>`; mobile SDKs are added to the native shell. Verify events fire correctly after conversion.
</Accordion>

<Accordion title="Can I convert back if I don't like the result?">
Yes. Conversion doesn't delete your original deployment. If the converted app isn't right, continue working on your original or start a new conversion job with clearer instructions.
</Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>

---

## Best practices for smooth conversion

- **Test edge cases**: empty states, long text, landscape orientation (mobile), narrow browser windows (web).
- **Check authentication flows**: login, signup, password reset and OAuth redirects must work on the new platform.
- **Verify file uploads**: ensure camera roll access (mobile) or drag-and-drop (web) works as expected.
- **Review navigation**: make sure every screen is reachable and back/close buttons behave correctly.
- **Test on real devices**: simulators are helpful, but real iOS/Android devices (or real browsers for web) catch platform quirks.

<Tip>
After conversion, open the app in preview and click through every major user flow. If something feels off, describe the issue in chat — the agent can fine-tune layout, navigation or component behavior.
</Tip>
